title: Differential Bounds for Fixed Nonzero FAST Differences
summary: FAST’s current differential analysis uses abstract difference behavior; deriving bounds for arbitrary fixed nonzero differences remains open.

formal_statement.body: For the differential analysis of FAST's format-preserving encryption and tokenization construction, extend the method so that it retains and analyzes arbitrary fixed nonzero differences in $Z_a$, rather than using only the abstract difference behavior currently considered. The unresolved task is to derive corresponding differential bounds for these arbitrary nonzero differences, despite the fact that a direct analysis would require forming $((a+1)^\ell-1)\times((a+1)^\ell-1)$ matrices, which cannot be formed. [S1]

scope.domain: Differential cryptanalysis of FAST format-preserving encryption and tokenization.
parameters: a: indexes the difference domain Z_a and appears in the direct-analysis matrix dimension
ell: exponent governing the direct-analysis matrix dimension
scope.unresolved_remainder: Derive differential bounds for arbitrary fixed nonzero differences in Z_a without forming the direct-analysis matrices that cannot be formed.

citations.label: FAST: Secure and High Performance Format-Preserving Encryption and Tokenization

progress.summary: The source presents arbitrary fixed nonzero differences as an unresolved extension of FAST’s abstract differential analysis. It identifies the required direct-analysis matrix size as the obstacle.
citation_labels: F. Betül Durak et al., FAST: Secure and High Performance Format-Preserving Encryption and Tokenization
